task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 4, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update about Alder Span Bank's branch consolidation, focusing on how the replacement services will work for customers who still need a counter.

facts.text: Alder Span Bank said Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026, that its Elwick and North Nettle branches will close Nov. 6.
Both branches will be consolidated into the bank's larger counter service in Fair Alder, 11 miles from Elwick and 17 miles from North Nettle.
The bank will retain a cash-dispensing ATM at each closing branch but neither machine will accept deposits.
A mobile counter is scheduled to visit each town two mornings a week starting Nov. 9.
Mobile-counter customers can deposit cash, obtain cashier's checks and meet an employee about account problems.
The mobile service's daily business-deposit cutoff will be noon, compared with 4 p.m. at the existing branches.
The two branches employ 14 people; ten have been offered jobs in Fair Alder and four on the mobile service.
The bank said it would pay employees' additional commuting costs for six months but would not say how many accepted transfers.
Bank records show counter transactions at the two branches fell from 42,000 in 2023 to 29,400 in 2025, a 30% decline.
The records count transactions, not distinct visits or customers, and do not identify which customers can use online banking.
Chief operating officer Mira Doss said the bank expects to save $460,000 annually after the first year of consolidation.
The estimate includes operating the mobile counter but excludes any proceeds from a possible sale of the bank-owned Elwick building; no sale price has been supplied.
Elwick hardware-store owner Benno Keel deposits cash after closing his shop at 1 p.m. on Saturdays.
Keel said the mobile timetable would require a change to his deposit routine or a trip to Fair Alder.
Keel said, "The money may move on a screen, but somebody still has to take my till to the bank."
The Elwick senior center has asked for an appointment system for the mobile counter; none has been announced.
Doss said, "We are reducing buildings, not eliminating the need to speak to a person."
The bank will hold customer information sessions in both towns during September; account numbers will not change.
The bank owns the Elwick building, which opened as a bank in 1968, but rents the North Nettle storefront.
The announcement does not change existing loan interest rates, and it gives no schedule for closing any other branch.
